sources.notes: Browser parser/path API. Complex-script shaping and rasterizer behavior should not be assumed identical to a browser shaping engine.
Pair positioning can implement kerning; class-based and contextual positioning can be more complex than simple pair tables.
Legacy kern table stores pair adjustments; CFF fonts rely on GPOS for kerning.

assumptions: The font parser resolves the font’s kerning implementation for the selected glyph pair.
licensing_data_restrictions: No user content is transmitted by normal tool execution. Third-party libraries retain their upstream licenses; font/PDF licensing remains the user’s responsibility.
uncertainty: This is sample-pair inspection, not exhaustive expansion of all class/context kerning. Browser shaping can differ because script, language and feature resolution may affect positioning.
